correctness.rationale: For nonnegative inputs the maximal map is represented by independent row choices; its norm is the largest selector norm because every selector is dominated coordinatewise on nonnegative inputs, and its top singular input may be chosen nonnegative. The hub-singleton/all-triangle selector has the two-dimensional constant-outer block given in the source, with Gram trace (2m+13)/9 and determinant 4/9. Its other singular sectors have squared norms at most 4/9. The positive row-Gram eigenvector (r,1,…,1) satisfies 1<r<3 and λr=r+2m/3. For m≥5, comparison to this vector works row by row: triangle rows have same-pair overlaps at most 1/3 and other-triangle overlaps at most 1/9; global rows have weighted sum (r+2m)/(2m+1); leaf singleton rows are bounded by 4/3+(2m−2+r)/(2m+1)<7/3<λ₅; the hub singleton is bounded by λr. For m=4 and a singleton hub the leaf singleton bound drops to 2. With a global hub the all-ones row comparison gives at most 19/9<λ₄, with the triangle and global rows bounded by 13/9 and one. The m=1,2,3 threshold tests were reproduced independently for all 18, 162 and 1,458 labeled selectors, using the symmetric shifted Gram characteristic coefficients in the exact quadratic field. Nonnegative coefficients of the monic det(xI+λI−AAᵀ) preclude a positive root, exactly the required bound, since eigenvalues are real. The original checker uses the same exact test with a scaling and removes only permutations of whole pairs, retaining both orders within a pair. The right singular input h/a=(9λ−4)/2 activates the stated selector; expanding the radical gives the stated asymptotic.
residual_risks: The exhaustive exact computations cover only m≤3. The higher-m bound is justified separately by the analytic row comparisons.
The input attains the norm but the result does not classify all maximizing inputs.

evidence: The graph is the windmill of triangles or cone over a matching, not a star: each outer vertex has one paired neighbor, so its local ball is of size three rather than two.
For m=1 this is K₃ and Corollary 5 gives exactly √(4/3). Record 64e84c2d1e15 has the same graph but an edge-variation heat-flow norm instead of a centered vertex maximal norm.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The exact equivalence at m=1 is credited. Changing the star by adding a matching changes the actual averaging rows, and a heat-flow estimate for the same graph is not a determination of this norm.

The m=1 complete-graph benchmark and general existence of centered finite graph maximal inequalities are credited to prior work. The closest different graph/operator claims and exact star result do not determine these norms. The search establishes a bounded statement-level distinction, not priority over all possible windmill or cone formulations.

value.rationale: Friendship graphs are a natural companion to stars and wheels in which a common hub combines with nontrivial local averaging inside each pair. An all-size sharp Hilbert norm, a matching input and its exact asymptotic clarify the effect of the local triangles; the value is not just a new small example or numerical spectral guess.
residual_risks: No assertion for arbitrary windmills, weighted graphs, other exponents or the uncentered operator.
